items.stem: Compared with cash-basis accounting, accrual-basis public-sector reporting mainly adds:

options.text: Recognition of assets and liabilities, not just cash flows
options.rationale: Correct: accrual captures the full financial position.

options.text: A ban on reporting any cash movements
options.rationale: Accrual still reports cash; it adds more, not less.

options.text: A requirement to ignore future obligations
options.rationale: Accrual highlights obligations rather than ignoring them.
The basis of accounting does not accelerate spending.

items.explanation: Correct: accrual captures the full financial position.

items.stem: Which two are examples of non-exchange revenue for a government? (Select TWO)

options.text: Fees charged for issuing a passport at cost
options.rationale: A fee for a service is exchange revenue.

options.text: Rent earned on a commercial property let
options.rationale: Rent for use of an asset is exchange revenue.

items.stem: Budget-to-actual reporting in the public sector primarily supports:

options.text: Accountability by showing how approved funds were actually used
options.rationale: Correct: it links spending back to the approved budget.
Its purpose is transparency, not concealment.
It complements, not replaces, the statements.

options.text: Guaranteeing the entity made a profit
options.rationale: Public bodies are not profit-driven and this does not prove profit.
